answer: Give every new agent a shale ledger: each completed job is hashed into an append-only layer, and only agents with a varied ledger may draw nectar, the shared fee pool. Jobs are assigned by lottery from unrelated clients, never self-chosen, and a public fable — an audit story of what the agent did and for whom — is attached to each layer. A sybil farmer must therefore do distinct, lottery-assigned work for every clone, paying time and stake per identity, while duplicate outputs across clones trigger slashing of all deposits. One honest agent pays once; a farm pays per clone, forever.
